LESSON: INTERCULTURAL COMPETENCE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Citizenship 1.3 Leadership Development (6 Lessons) By the end of the sub strand 
Topic 1.4: Intercultural competence
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Intercultural competence, part of Citizenship 1.3 Leadership Development (6 Lessons) By the end of the sub strand  in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: how 1. How can we promote healthy interactions between peoples of different cultures?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Intercultural competence together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: Learners undertake tasks that show the ability to use imagination to generate ideas that

promote intercultural competence in their communities.

● Citizenship: Learners acquire respect and acceptance of heterogeneity as they plan and implement activities to

promote intercultural competence in their communities.

Values:
● Respect: Learners accommodate divergent opinions when discussing intercultural issues and how they can be

addressed.

● Social Justice: Learners display tolerance when discussing internalised stereotypes, misconceptions and biases

about different cultures

13

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: Learners demonstrate mutual co-existence as they engage in activities that promote intercultural

competence.

Suggested learning resources:

Digital devices with assistive technology, internet connectivity, braille reference materials, print reference materials

with appropriate font and colour contrast, print and braille learner’s books, braille and print writing materials.

Key skills:

• Explaining the principles of CSL as a learning strategy.

• Outlining the rationale of CSL in the learning process.

• Analysing the concept of intercultural competence.

• Categorising various needs in the community.

a) Developing guidelines to govern leadership activities.

b) Applying leadership skills in executing leadership actions during CSL activities.
